To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

canine aplastic sera contain a factor(s) that stimulates human megakaryocytic progenitors to form colonies composed of larger, more polyploid megakaryocytes, but that increasing the concentration of such sera favors mitosis over endomitosis and thereby inhibits the development of megaspherocytes.
the mitotic and the endomitotic events that occur in human megakaryaocyte development in vitro may be influenced by factors in aplastic canine sera.

canine sera from irradiation-induced aplastic dogs stimulate both the mitotic phase of human megakayocyte development in vitro and that the mitotic phase is favored over endoreduplication at high serum concentrations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an in vitro assay for human megakaryopoiesis.
the interrelationship between mitosis (cell proliferation) and endomitosis (endoreduplication) during human megakaryocytic development.

the identification of the factors in aplastic canine sera that promote the development of megacaryocyte colonies in vitro and with the elucidation of their mechanism of action on human megakaryocytic development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mitotic and polyploid events in human megacaryocytopoietic development are interrelated.
the mitotic and/or endomitotic phases in human megakayocyte development in vitro are influenced by the presence of a factor or factors in the aplastic canine sera.
the mitotic and the endomitotic events are both influenced by the same serum factors, and that these are the same serum factors which stimulate megakaryocytoiesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mitotic and the endomitotic events are interrelated and that the endomitosis is not an independent process.

megakaryocyte polyploidization is a function of the number of cell divisions that occur prior to the onset of endomitosis, and the mitotic prior cell history may be regulated by the in vitro concentration of a canine serum factor or factors that are present in aplastic sera.
the mitotic phase of human megakaryaocytopoieses may be influenced by factors present in aplasic canine serum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the megakaryocyte precursor cell is not a static cell but is a dynamic cell that is capable of responding to its microenvironment.
the megakaryocyte precursor cells are not all equal, and the size of their end products is not necessarily related to the number of times that they divide.
the mitotic and polyploidization phases of human megkaryocyte development are not independent events but are interrelated.
